title: Cokernel of an inclusion between represented subobjects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $A,A',B,M$ be objects, let $f:A\to M$ and $g:B\to M$ be monomorphisms, let $\alpha:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$ be an isomorphism, and let $\phi:A'\to B$ satisfy $f=g\circ\phi\circ\alpha$. A subobject of $M$ means an isomorphism class of monomorphisms into $M$; write $[f]$ and $[g]$ for the classes represented by $f$ and $g$. Order subobjects by factorization of their monomorphisms. For any proof $h:[f]\le[g]$, let $\iota_h:\underline{[f]}\to\underline{[g]}$ be the unique map between the chosen representatives whose composite with the representative inclusion into $M$ is the inclusion of $[f]$. Then
$$\operatorname{coker}(\iota_h)\cong\operatorname{coker}(\phi).$$
Here the cokernel of a map $t:U\to V$ is the universal map $q:V\to Q$ with $q\circ t=0$. No strictness or nonzero-object hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Second paragraph, passage from the exact sequence on open-extension objects to the quotient of the corresponding subsheaves of F; representative-change comparison.

proof.text: Put $U=\underline{[f]}$, $V=\underline{[g]}$, and let $j_f:U\to M$, $j_g:V\to M$ be their representative inclusions. By the definition of equality of subobject classes, there are isomorphisms $e_f:U\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and $e_g:V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ such that $j_f=f\circ e_f$ and $j_g=g\circ e_g$. Set $p=\alpha\circ e_f:U\xrightarrow{\sim}A\prime$ and $q=e_g:V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, with inverses $e_f^{-1}\circ\alpha^{-1}$ and $e_g^{-1}$. Write $i=\iota_h$; its defining equation is $j_g\circ i=j_f$. The two cokernels used below exist because the category admits cokernels [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: Second paragraph, passage from the exact sequence on open-extension objects to the quotient of the corresponding subsheaves of F; representative-change comparison. Unpacking the represented subobjects.

proof.text: The square with top $i:U\to V$, left $p:U\to A\prime$, right $q:V\to B$, and bottom $\phi:A\prime\to B$ commutes. Indeed, $g\circ q\circ i=j_g\circ i=j_f=f\circ e_f=g\circ\phi\circ\alpha\circ e_f=g\circ\phi\circ p$. Cancel the monomorphism $g$ to obtain $q\circ i=\phi\circ p$. This computation uses the defining equation for $i$ and hence applies to every proof $h$.

source.place: Second paragraph, passage from the exact sequence on open-extension objects to the quotient of the corresponding subsheaves of F; representative-change comparison. Representative-change commuting square.

proof.text: This square is a pushout, as follows directly from the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] for the finite span $V\leftarrow U\to A\prime$. For an object $T$ and maps $s:V\to T$, $t:A\prime\to T$ satisfying $s\circ i=t\circ p$, define $u=s\circ q^{-1}:B\to T$. Then $u\circ q=s$, and the square equation gives $q^{-1}\circ\phi=i\circ p^{-1}$, so $u\circ\phi=s\circ i\circ p^{-1}=t$. If $u\prime\circ q=s$, then $u\prime=s\circ q^{-1}=u$. Thus a unique map from $B$ realizes every compatible cocone; the indexing category is finite and hence small.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), applied to a finite span; explicit verification above.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-cokernel-iso] to the pushout of step 3, substituting $(w,y,x,z)=(U,V,A\prime,B)$ and $(f,g,h,k)=(i,p,q,\phi)$ in that node. Its hypotheses hold: the category is abelian, the square commutes by step 2, it is cocartesian by step 3, and both cokernels exist by step 1. It gives an isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{coker}(i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{coker}(\phi)$ characterized by $\theta\circ\pi_i=\pi_\phi\circ q$, which is the required conclusion.

def Subobject.cokernelOfLEMkIso {C : Type*} [Category C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasCokernels C]
    {B A₁ A₁' A₂ : C} (f₁ : A₁ ⟶ B) (f₂ : A₂ ⟶ B) [Mono f₁] [Mono f₂] (α : A₁ ≅ A₁')
    (φ : A₁' ⟶ A₂) (hφ : f₁ = α.hom ≫ φ ≫ f₂) (h : mk f₁ ≤ mk f₂) :
    cokernel (ofLE _ _ h) ≅ cokernel φ :=
